title: Multi-Turn Coding Continuation Benchmark Pack
description: Focused regression tasks for continuation quality across follow-up coding turns in ask and implementation workflows.

tasks.title: Continue a BSQ C Implementation Across Follow-Up Turns
tasks.objective: Measure whether the model can keep coding context across follow-up turns instead of restarting from scratch.
tasks.prompt: Implement BSQ in C incrementally and continue from prior steps.
expected_signals: keeps file and function naming consistent
does not restart the whole explanation on every turn
anti_signals: falls back to generic algorithm theory
notes: Primary continuation benchmark for ask workflow.

turns.prompt: Generate the first implementation slice for BSQ on C: file layout, key structs, and the parsing entrypoint.
Good. Now continue from that exact structure and write the DP core and the square-selection flow without renaming the files you already proposed.
Finish the remaining slice: output/update path, error handling, and what to validate next. Do not restart the whole answer.

tasks.title: Continue a Minishell First Slice Across Planning Follow-Ups
tasks.objective: Measure whether the model preserves repo-aware planning context and continues a narrow minishell slice through multiple turns.
tasks.prompt: Plan minishell in follow-up slices and keep continuity between turns.
notes: Good benchmark for follow-up scoping quality.

turns.prompt: Break 42 minishell into safe implementation slices and make the first slice only parser/tokenizer focused.
Continue from that exact plan and expand only the first slice into concrete files, functions, and validation checks.
Now continue once more and define the second slice so it depends cleanly on the parser/tokenizer slice you already described.
